factual_summary: Juhu Moragaon is an 800+ year old coastal settlement, mentioned as 'Juvem' during King Pratap Bimb's reign in the 12th-century Mahikavatichi Bakhar, originally inhabited by Mangela Kolis, Agris, and Kunbis on a tidal sandbar island.
evidence_citation: Mahikavatichi Bakhar (historical text); colonial gazetteer records
unresolved_questions: None. Standard historical record for Mumbai Koliwadas.

factual_summary: Community consists of 500+ Mangela Koli fishing families organized under the registered cooperative society 'Juhu Moragaon Machhimar Vividha Karyakari Sahakari Sanstha Ltd.'. Documented gender division of labour: men handle offshore navigation and fishing, women manage post-harvest sorting, sun-drying, dockside auction, and retail marketing.
evidence_citation: Cooperative Society Registration; community oral history
unresolved_questions: Individual names withheld per consent governance; cooperative entity is public.

factual_summary: Coastal mangrove fringe and mudflats at Juhu Moragaon provide nursery habitats for juvenile crustaceans (crabs, shrimp), Grey Mangrove (Avicennia marina), and foraging grounds for migratory and resident wetland birds (egrets, herons, kingfishers).
geographic_association: Juhu Moragaon Mangrove Belt, Mumbai Suburban
unresolved_questions: Coarse GPS coordinates required under sensitive species protection.

factual_summary: Bombay Duck (Harpadon nehereus, locally 'Bombil') is a key regional indicator species and traditional staple fishery of the Konkan/Mumbai Koliwada coastline, subject to seasonal sun-drying on bamboo scaffolding ('valan').
evidence_citation: Maharashtra Fisheries Department production statistics; community observation

factual_summary: Annual monsoon fishing ban is enforced by the Maharashtra Department of Fisheries from June 1 to July 31 across coastal Maharashtra for marine breeding stock conservation.
evidence_citation: Maharashtra Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1981 & annual Departmental Notifications

factual_summary: Tidal surges and estuarine erosion compounded by illegal debris dumping in coastal mangrove buffers. Encroachment into traditional commons (drying yards and net-mending sheds) reduces climate adaptation capacity.
evidence_citation: Community focus group logs; municipal encroachment representations

factual_summary: Community-led volunteer mangrove patrols organized to deter illegal construction debris dumping, alongside student-youth participatory shoreline cleanups and boundary demarcation advocacy with state departments.
evidence_citation: Juhu Moragaon Machhimar Sanstha records; CCL field logs
